key_insight: A superconducting qubit can be used to deterministically and programmably generate multipartite entanglement across multiple mechanical phonon modes, including W, GHZ, and cluster states.
engineering_relevance: This shows a scalable route to on-chip mechanical quantum memories and sensors that can exploit long-lived multimode resonators for quantum information processing and multiparameter sensing.
method: Sequentially apply optimal-control-engineered isometries between a transmon qubit and successive mechanical modes.
Prepare matrix product states of bond dimension two in a high-overtone bulk acoustic wave resonator.
Use correlated-noise sensing and state tomography to characterize entanglement and dephasing.
evidence_signal: The paper reports full quantum state tomography and certification of genuine multipartite entanglement among up to four modes, plus quantitative bounds on collective dephasing from sensing experiments.
watch_item: Scalability may be constrained by control complexity, mode-dependent decoherence, and maintaining high-fidelity qubit-to-mode transfer as the number of entangled modes grows.
paper_title: Deterministic and programmable generation of mechanical multipartite entangled states
